title: Broken Trust
theme: Cheating. Catching. Confronting. R&B has never shied away from infidelity — from Billy Paul's unapologetic affair to Destiny's Child's precision trap. The songs that exposed what happens when trust breaks down.
narrativePurpose: Test knowledge of the R&B catalog built around infidelity — the songs that caught cheaters, confronted betrayal, and turned personal devastation into some of the most commercially and artistically significant recordings of the past five decades.
toneProgression: The infidelity anthems everyone knows → the producers, labels, and personal stories behind the recordings → the archival connections and creative genealogy that link decades of broken-trust R&B

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 2-0-0-0 — the year Destiny's Child's 'Say My Name' and Toni Braxton's 'He Wasn't Man Enough' were among the defining sounds of R&B, both confronting betrayal directly. The year 2000: when R&B stopped making excuses for cheaters.

questions.question: Destiny's Child's 'Say My Name' (2000) — in which catching a cheating partner is built into the chorus itself — appeared on which album?

metadata.fact: 'Say My Name' was the third single from Destiny's Child's second studio album 'The Writing's on the Wall,' released on July 27, 1999.
metadata.storyHook: The writing was literally on the wall. Destiny's Child built the trap into the song itself — if he won't say your name, you know why.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Say My Name' appeared on The Writing's on the Wall (1999). questions.question: Billy Paul's 1972 soul classic 'Me and Mrs. Jones' — a candid portrait of an extramarital affair at a regular café meeting — was written and produced primarily by which Philadelphia soul duo?

metadata.fact: 'Me and Mrs. Jones' was written by Kenny Gamble, Leon Huff, and Cary Gilbert, and produced by Gamble and Huff for Philadelphia International Records.
metadata.storyHook: Gamble and Huff made the sounds of Philadelphia. Billy Paul made the most unashamed affair song in soul history.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Me and Mrs. Jones' written by Kenny Gamble, Leon Huff, and Cary Gilbert. Source: Facebook song summary post https://www.facebook.com/RobertLevEy2/posts/me-and-mrs-jones-is-a-1972-soul-song-written-by-kenny-gamble-leon-huff-and-cary-/816

questions.question: TLC's 1994 hit 'Creep' — in which the narrator justifies a secret relationship because her partner is also unfaithful — was produced by which Atlanta-based hitmaker who shaped TLC's early sound?

metadata.fact: Dallas Austin wrote and produced 'Creep' and was a key architect of TLC's early commercial sound throughout the early 1990s.
metadata.storyHook: Dallas Austin built TLC's sound. 'Creep' turned it into one of the decade's most frank conversations about infidelity.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Dallas Austin produced 'Creep.' Source: YouTube interview https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ti7gqTkSSTc

questions.question: Brandy and Monica's 1998 duet 'The Boy Is Mine' — a confrontation between two women over the same man — became one of the longest-running #1 hits on the Billboard Hot 100. How many consecutive weeks did it spend at the top?

metadata.fact: 'The Boy Is Mine' spent 13 consecutive weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — at the time the third-longest-running #1 in US chart history.
metadata.storyHook: Thirteen weeks. Two women. One man who wasn't worth either of them.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'The Boy Is Mine' spent 13 consecutive weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Boy_Is_Mine_(Brandy_and_Monica_song), Instagram reel https://www.instagram.com/reel/DX6tZ-qo4xa/

questions.question: The O'Jays' 1972 album 'Back Stabbers' — anchored by its infidelity-themed title track — also contained which song that became the group's first and only #1 on the Billboard Hot 100?

metadata.fact: 'Love Train' — from the Back Stabbers album — reached #1 on both the R&B Singles and Hot 100 charts and was The O'Jays' first and only #1 on the US pop chart.
metadata.storyHook: The same album that called out back stabbers also produced a message of universal love. The O'Jays contained multitudes.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Love Train' was on the Back Stabbers album and was The O'Jays' first and only Hot 100 #1. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Train

questions.question: Kelis's furious 1999 debut single 'Caught Out There' — featuring the repeatedly screamed 'I hate you so much right now' — was produced by which duo whose experimental sound defined late-1990s R&B?

metadata.fact: 'Caught Out There' was produced by The Neptunes (Pharrell Williams and Chad Hugo), whose alien-textured arrangements gave Kelis's debut album 'Kaleidoscope' its distinctive sound.
metadata.storyHook: The Neptunes built the world 'Caught Out There' lives in. Kelis burned it down.

questions.question: Most Philadelphia International Records sessions — including 'Me and Mrs. Jones' and 'Back Stabbers' — were recorded at which Philadelphia studio that became the sonic home of 1970s soul?

metadata.fact: Sigma Sound Studios, founded in 1968 by Joe Tarsia, was the home of 'The Philly Sound' — where MFSB and countless PIR artists recorded their defining work.
metadata.storyHook: Sigma Sound Studios. Every signature riff, every lush string arrangement, every Philadelphia International hit. It started in that room.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Sigma Sound Studios was the primary recording facility for Philadelphia International Records. Source: PhillySound.org https://www.phillysound.org/sigma-sound-studios

sources.title: Sigma Sound Studios – PhillySound.org

questions.question: Destiny's Child's 'Say My Name' was recorded by the original four-member lineup — but two members left before the music video was filmed. LeToya Luckett and LaTavia Roberson were replaced by which two singers?

metadata.fact: Michelle Williams and Farrah Franklin replaced Luckett and Roberson. The public discrepancy between the album credits and the music video made the lineup change immediately controversial.
metadata.storyHook: The credits said one thing. The video showed another. Destiny's Child had replaced two members mid-hit.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: LeToya Luckett and LaTavia Roberson were replaced by Michelle Williams and Farrah Franklin. questions.question: Monica — Brandy's counterpart on 'The Boy Is Mine' — was signed to which label, a Dallas Austin–founded imprint distributed through Arista, during her commercial peak?

metadata.fact: Producer Dallas Austin offered Monica a record deal with Rowdy Records — his Arista-distributed imprint — which released her debut album 'Miss Thang' and her breakthrough recordings.
metadata.storyHook: Dallas Austin built the label. Monica filled it with hits. Rowdy Records was the launchpad for one of the 1990s' most important R&B voices.

metadata.fact: 'Confessions Part II' was written by Usher, Bryan-Michael Cox, and Jermaine Dupri, who also produced the track. Dupri was central to Usher's commercial peak as head of So So Def Recordings.

questions.question: Kelis — who raged about infidelity in 'Caught Out There' — grew up in which New York City borough?

questions.question: 'Say My Name' was produced by Rodney Jerkins, one of the late 1990s' most in-demand producers. That same producer had previously produced which Whitney Houston infidelity anthem — which won the Grammy for Best R&B Song in 2000?
choices: It's Not Right But It's Okay

metadata.song: It's Not Right But It's Okay
topicTags: It's Not Right But It's Okay
metadata.fact: Rodney Jerkins produced Whitney Houston's 'It's Not Right But It's Okay' (1998) — a woman's furious response to discovering her partner's infidelity. The song won the Grammy Award for Best R&B Song at the 2000 ceremony.
metadata.storyHook: The same producer who caught the cheater in 'Say My Name' also helped Whitney Houston tell her cheating partner exactly where he could go.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Rodney Jerkins produced 'It's Not Right But It's Okay'; the song won Best R&B Song at the 2000 Grammys. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s_Not_Right_but_It%27s_Okay

questions.question: TLC's 'Creep' was released during a turbulent period for Left Eye. Her volatile relationship with which Atlanta Falcons wide receiver culminated in a 1994 arson incident that made international headlines?

metadata.fact: Left Eye's relationship with Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Andre Rison was intensely publicized. In June 1994, she set fire to his Atlanta mansion — resulting in criminal charges — while TLC was at the height of their commercial success.
metadata.storyHook: The year 'Creep' was everywhere, Left Eye was in the news for something else entirely. Her relationship with Andre Rison gave 1994 one of its most dramatic stories.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Left Eye had a relationship with Andre Rison and was involved in the 1994 fire at his mansion — a widely documented public record. Sources: REVOLT TV https://www.revolt.tv/article/tboz-opens-up-sickle-cell-healthcare-advocacy-prep, Lisa Lopes Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Lopes
metadata.hostNote: This question references a documented criminal incident involving a deceased artist. HOST_SENSITIVITY: handle with care in live delivery. The question is factual and historically documented.
